claims.text: The alloy is equimolar WTaTiVZr.
WTaTiVZr has enhanced plastic strain relative to commercially pure tungsten at high temperature.
WTaTiVZr has enhanced toughness relative to commercially pure tungsten at high temperature.
The enhanced plastic strain and toughness are primarily governed by a fine-scale dual-phase microstructure with semi-coherent interfaces.
Lattice distortions introduced by Ta, Ti, V, and Zr generate the semi-coherent interfaces.
The semi-coherent interfaces are preferential sites for dislocation nucleation at high temperature.
The semi-coherent interfaces enhance dynamic recovery at high temperature.
Interface-mediated dislocation activity produces more extensive work hardening.
Interface-mediated deformation delays crack propagation.
Powder-metallurgy- or arc-melted WTaTiVZr is expected to possess a fine-grained multiphase microstructure consisting predominantly of a BCC matrix and secondary phases or interfacial features.
Commercially pure tungsten has a relatively coarse, homogeneous, single-phase microstructure.
The alloying additions promote formation of secondary phases or interfaces that lower barriers to dislocation nucleation.
Enhanced dislocation nucleation and dynamic recovery increase plastic deformation and fracture-energy absorption.
WTaTiVZr should have a lower yield stress than pure tungsten under the specified test conditions.
WTaTiVZr should have significantly greater plastic strain to failure and fracture toughness than pure tungsten.
Deformed WTaTiVZr should show enhanced dislocation activity at semi-coherent interfaces and microcrack blunting.
The coarse homogeneous microstructure of pure tungsten promotes early crack initiation and limited dislocation mobility.
The proposed mechanism applies at 800–1200 °C under moderate irradiation conditions representative of plasma-facing components.
The mechanism may not apply at low temperature or extreme strain rates because other deformation mechanisms can dominate.
Multiphase interfaces enhance ductility in related refractory-alloy systems.
